scope: Int32 CPU tensor captures and results through nested workers, typed task layouts, cached outcomes, retained owners and fault/cancellation settlement.

semantics.types: Generated task tensor layout keys and private IDs include numeric element identity and rank. Int32 and float32 layouts remain distinct despite identical physical memref descriptor sizes.
semantics.ownership: Existing generated retain/copy callbacks retain backing dependencies before descriptor publication. Cached awaits/observations can retain independent owners. Runtime/scheduler code unchanged.
semantics.lifetimes: Returned tensor bits are verified after task outcomes, all worker threads and the core are destroyed; an independent immutable lease is verified again after its receiving Invocation is destroyed.
semantics.arithmetic_and_errors: Checked MLIR arithmetic unchanged. Supervised arithmetic faults preserve source location and FaultKind.Arithmetic; handlers can reuse parent tensors and start another group. Shape and absent-payload error paths retain existing checks.
semantics.admission_and_cancellation: Byte-budget admission rejection, invocation allocation-failure sweeps and explicit cancellation/deadline signals use the existing bounded scheduler. No wall-clock deadline feature or new scheduling policy.
semantics.test_interface: Private --test-entry in a task module exposes a const TaskEntry pointer named kalandra_task_test_entry for a parameterless numeric source function. Native tests drive it through TaskCore. Arbitrary task inputs and a public foreign/wire ABI are not introduced.
semantics.remaining: Integer reductions/matmul, additional source numeric types, conversions and GPU integer arithmetic remain gated. CLI main still requires a scalar result.
